summary: Idaho County site: platform tower and cabin in 1922 (End Butte page) or a 20 ft tower and cabin in 1937 (1981 history); manned to 1941, then dropped; listed as gone.

facts.design: 20-foot observation tower and a cabin of peeled logs, about 8 by 10 feet, with a split cedar shake roof (1981 history)
facts.status_note: Listed as a platform that is gone; no source describes what, if anything, remains at the point
facts.agency: Nez Perce National Forest, per the Idaho County list

events.note: Platform tower and log cabin at Rhoda Point, per the End Butte page; conflicts with the 1937 start in the 1981 history
Tower and cabin built the season the point was first manned, per the 1981 history
The 1981 history says the point was first manned in 1937
Daland Broker manned the point in the 1938 and 1939 seasons
Manned through the 1941 season, then dropped from the fire plan

evidence.supports: county list places Rhoda Point in the Nez Perce National Forest
Rhoda Point listed under Idaho County
1981 history is the source of the account
evidence.quote: Louis Hartig, 'Historic Facilities of the Lochsa Ranger District' - 1981
The first time that this emergency lookout was ever manned was in 1937

evidence.supports: Ranger Millard Evenson in charge of the district in 1937
evidence.quote: Ranger Millard Evenson was in charge of the district

evidence.supports: William Pointer and two-man crew built a telephone line from End Butte to Rhoda Point in 1937
evidence.quote: That year William Pointer and a two man crew built a telephone line from End Butte out to Rhoda Point.

evidence.supports: 20-foot observation tower on a boulder-strewn hilltop
evidence.quote: on a boulder-strewn hilltop they built a 20-foot-high observation tower

evidence.supports: cabin of peeled logs with split cedar shake roof, short distance from tower
evidence.quote: A short distance from the tower they built a cabin of peeled logs with a split cedar shake roof.

evidence.supports: cabin about 8 by 10 feet, mainly for off-season storage of camp equipment
evidence.quote: The cabin was only about 8x10 feet in size and was primarily for off-season storage of camp equipment

evidence.supports: cabin also used for sleeping quarters
evidence.quote: It was also used for sleeping quarters by the lookout man.
Cooking was done under a tent and fly out front.

evidence.supports: Daland Broker manned the point in the 1938 and 1939 seasons
evidence.quote: Daland Broker manned the point during the 1938-39 seasons.

evidence.supports: manned through 1941, then dropped from the fire plan
evidence.quote: The lookout was manned through the 1941 season then dropped from the fire plan.

evidence.supports: 1922 platform tower and log cabin at Rhoda Point, about two miles southeast of End Butte camp
evidence.quote: 1922 – Camp at End Butte, also a platform tower and log cabin 2 miles southeast at Rhoda Point

evidence.supports: Rhoda Point listed as platform, status gone

notes_for_editor: Two accounts of the start do not match: the End Butte page says a platform tower and log cabin stood at Rhoda Point in 1922, while the 1981 history (quoted on the Idaho County list) says the point was first manned in 1937 and that the crew built the tower and cabin then. Not resolved; the 1922 structure may be a different one, but no source says so. The 1981 history is attributed to Louis Hartig on the county list; the End Butte page spells the name Harting. Record coordinates and status (gone) match the Forest Fire Lookout Association list. No source found on current condition or access.
